title: choose-tree format prints wrong values for external commands
body:
### Issue description

When the choose-tree format contains an invocation of an external command, the result of that command for the **last** choose-tree item is printed on **every** line in the choose tree. 

Using only internal identifiers such as `pane_pid`, there is no problem. For example: 

`bind-key s choose-tree -sZ -O name -F #{pane_pid}"`
                                                                                                                                                       
    (0)   + cURL-1: 506069                                                                                                                             
    (1)   + cURL-2: 506104                                                                                                                             
    (2)   + experimental-1: 506168                                                                                                                     
    (3)   + fausec-1: 506235                                                                                                                           
    (4)   + fausec-2: 506304                                                                                                                           
    (5)   + logging-1: 506398                                                                                                                          
    (6)   + logging-2: 506464                                                                                                                          
    (7)   + mbedtls-1: 506581                                                                                                                          
    (8)   + repo-1: 506665                                                                                                                             
    (9)   + root-1: 506754                                                                                                                             
    (M-a) + shell-1: 506823                                                                                                                            
    (M-b) + shell-2: 506931                                                                                                                            
    (M-c) + validator-1: 507027                                                                                                                        
    (M-d) + vm-1: 507106                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                       
But if an external command such as `echo` is invoked in the choose-tree format, the **last line's value** for that command is applied to every line. For example

`bind-key s choose-tree -sZ -O name -F "#(echo #{pane_pid})"`

    (0)   + cURL-1: 507106                                                                                                                             
    (1)   + cURL-2: 507106                                                                                                                             
    (2)   + experimental-1: 507106                                                                                                                     
    (3)   + fausec-1: 507106                                                                                                                           
    (4)   + fausec-2: 507106                                                                                                                           
    (5)   + logging-1: 507106                                                                                                                          
    (6)   + logging-2: 507106                                                                                                                          
    (7)   + mbedtls-1: 507106                                                                                                                          
    (8)   + repo-1: 507106                                                                                                                             
    (9)   + root-1: 507106                                                                                                                             
    (M-a) + shell-1: 507106                                                                                                                            
    (M-b) + shell-2: 507106                                                                                                                            
    (M-c) + validator-1: 507106                                                                                                                        
    (M-d) + vm-1: 507106                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                       
### Required information

Please provide the following information:

* tmux version 3.5a
* Platform: Linux unknown (actually Fedora 41, specifically `Linux fedora 6.13.6-200.fc41.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Mar  7 21:33:48 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux`)
* $TERM inside: tmux-256color
* $TERM outside: xterm-256color

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This looks like it's by design.  The man page says this about `#()`:
```
     In addition, the last line of a shell command's output may be inserted using ‘#()’.  For example, ‘#(uptime)’ will
     insert the system's uptime.  When constructing formats, tmux does not wait for ‘#()’ commands to finish; instead,
     the previous result from running the same command is used, or a placeholder if the command has not been run before.
     If the command hasn't exited, the most recent line of output will be used, but the status line will not be updated
     more than once a second.  Commands are executed with the tmux global environment set (see the GLOBAL AND SESSION
     ENVIRONMENT section).
```
This makes it more obvious that this is happening:
```
tmux bind-key s choose-tree -sZ -O name -F "#(shuf -i 1-10000 -n 1)"
```
You can see a new random value is chosen every few seconds and it's used for all the lines.  You can't count on that shell command being executed once per line of output in `choose-tree`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Sounds like maybe this is more a feature request. Instead of running any specified shell commands while assembling the `choose-tree`, it would be sufficient to simply copy the exact string that last appeared on the session's `status-right`. With session status updated every N seconds, the user can decide how much cpu time to invest in keeping those current. For me, the cost is very low for 5 second updates, and even that is not really necessary.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I have some progress, maybe I fixed this...

First, using `FORMAT_PANE|wp->id` as the tag when wp!=NULL in format_create_defaults in format.c gets the pane_pid into the data. 

Then in `window_tree_build_window`:
```
          if (TAILQ_NEXT(wp, entry) == NULL) {
                  if (!window_tree_filter_pane(s, wl, wp, filter))
                          goto empty;
                  return (1);
          }
```

I removed the `return (1)` here and let the code continue.  If `TAILQ_NEXT` is true then there's exactly one item in the list and then if `window_tree_filter_pane` filters out that one item, it's empty, so the `goto empty` is appropriate.  But it seemed odd to return here even if there was only a single item.  Removing the return, I now I see the different PIDs from the echos:

```
(0) - 0: 206052
(1) ├─> - 0: 206052
(2) │   └─> 0: 206033
(3) └─> - 1: 206052
(4)     └─> 0: 206052 
```
This looks reasonable to me.  Is this the expected tree output with the format `"#(echo #{pane_pid})"`?

This is what `pstree` shows:
```
/usr/bin/pstree -ap 206032
tmux: server,206032
  ├─bash,206033
  └─bash,206052
```

Does this fix the issue?  Is the above 5 line output the expected output?  It looks like it based on my stepping through the code.  If this is good, I'll do a PR this evening.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The root is the `session`, then the next level is the `window` then the third level is the `window_pane`.  There is a `choose-buffer` command but it doesn't work for me in master as I compiled it, but it does work for me in the older version on debian.  I will look at that later.

You are using `#pane_pid` in the format for each line and at each level, this is the pid of a pane which is associated with that level in the tree.  The `pane_pid` is that of the shell inside the pane.  The root session has the first window and the first window_pane and thus the pid is that of the shell in that pane.  The window child of the session, again, has a window_pane and the pane_pid is the pid of that same shell (the shell that started the windows).  The third level is the pane itself and again it's the pid of the shell but in this case each window pane has its own shell so the 3rd level is the level I see with unique pids.  Is this also what you see?

Your example seems like it works with my fix but you're correct, it's messy with the session and window lines, but that does not appear to be a bug.

What about `choose-buffer`?  Does it work for you?  Is it more like what you are looking for?

comments.body:
The `#{pane_id}` for a window should be the pane ID of the active pane and for a session of the active pane in the current window, so I don't think this is fully correct.

Try this, for example:
~~~~
$ tmux -Ltest new -d \; neww \; splitw \; new -d \; new -d
$ tmux -Ltest lsp -aF '#{pane_id}'
%0
%1
%2
%3
%4
$ tmux -Ltest lsw -aF '#{pane_id}'
%0
%2
%3
%4
$ tmux -Ltest ls -F '#{pane_id}'
%2
%3
%4
~~~~
If you attach and do `choose-tree -F '#{pane_id}'` you will see the labels match this. The `#{pane_id}` expansion in `#()` should also.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: You wanted `pane_pid` but it should have the same behaviour as `pane_id`. Two sessions should not have the same `pane_pid` or `pane_id`, unless they have the same current window. Two windows will never have the same because a pane cannot be in two windows.
